nativeFormat.description: ArchInt lossless ArchiMate 4.0 model and view document

exchangeFormat.description: The Open Group ArchiMate Model Exchange File Format; no official 4.0 exchange schema is assumed

domains.name: Common
domains.description: Cross-domain behaviour, active structure, and composite concepts

domains.name: Business
domains.description: Business-specific actors, interfaces, objects, and products

domains.name: Application
domains.description: Software components, interfaces, and structured data

domains.name: Strategy
domains.description: Resources, capabilities, value streams, and courses of action

domains.name: Motivation
domains.description: The context and reasons behind the architecture

domains.name: Implementation and Migration
domains.description: Work packages, deliverables, and stable architecture plateaus

elements.name: Role
elements.description: A position or purpose an active structure has in performing behaviour

elements.name: Collaboration
elements.description: A collection of active structure elements working together

elements.name: Path
elements.description: A logical link through which active structure elements exchange information, data, energy, or material

elements.name: Service
elements.description: Explicitly defined behaviour provided to an environment

elements.name: Process
elements.description: A sequence of behaviours that achieves a specific result

elements.name: Function
elements.description: A collection of behaviour based on chosen criteria

elements.name: Event
elements.description: Something that happens or occurs, such as a state change

elements.name: Grouping
elements.description: A collection of concepts that belong together

elements.name: Location
elements.description: A place or position where structure can be located or behaviour performed

elements.name: Business Actor
elements.description: A business entity capable of performing behaviour

elements.name: Business Interface
elements.description: A point of access where a business actor makes services available

elements.name: Business Object
elements.description: A conceptual passive element relevant from a business perspective

elements.name: Product
elements.description: A coherent collection of services and passive structure offered as a whole

elements.name: Application Component
elements.description: An encapsulated software unit that performs application behaviour

elements.name: Application Interface
elements.description: A point of access where an application component exposes services

elements.name: Data Object
elements.description: Data structured for automated processing

elements.name: Node
elements.description: A generic IT or physical structure that hosts or interacts with other structures

elements.name: Device
elements.description: IT hardware used for processing, data storage, or similar purposes

elements.name: System Software
elements.description: Software providing an environment for storing, executing, and using software or data

elements.name: Technology Interface
elements.description: A point of access where technology structure exposes services

elements.name: Communication Network
elements.description: IT structures for transmission, routing, and reception of data

elements.name: Distribution Network
elements.description: A physical network used to transport materials or energy

elements.name: Equipment
elements.description: A physical machine, tool, instrument, or livestock

elements.name: Facility
elements.description: A physical structure or environment

elements.name: Artifact
elements.description: A physical piece of data used or produced in a process

elements.name: Material
elements.description: Tangible physical matter or energy

elements.name: Resource
elements.description: A useful or valuable possession or means available to the enterprise

elements.name: Capability
elements.description: An ability an organizational entity, person, or system possesses

elements.name: Value Stream
elements.description: A sequence of activities that creates an overall result for a customer or stakeholder

elements.name: Course of Action
elements.description: An approach or plan for configuring capabilities and resources to achieve a goal

elements.name: Stakeholder
elements.description: The perspective from which a business actor perceives architecture effects

elements.name: Driver
elements.description: An internal or external condition that motivates change

elements.name: Assessment
elements.description: A result of analysis of a driver or state of affairs

elements.name: Goal
elements.description: A high-level statement of intent, direction, or desired end state

elements.name: Outcome
elements.description: An end result, effect, or consequence of a state of affairs

elements.name: Principle
elements.description: A statement of intent defining a general property that applies in context

elements.name: Requirement
elements.description: A statement of need defining a property of a system

elements.name: Meaning
elements.description: Knowledge or expertise present in, or interpretation given to, a concept

elements.name: Value
elements.description: The relative worth, utility, or importance of a concept

elements.name: Work Package
elements.description: A series of actions designed to achieve results within constraints

elements.name: Deliverable
elements.description: A result of a work package

elements.name: Plateau
elements.description: A relatively stable state of the architecture during a limited period

elements.name: And Junction
elements.description: A junction that requires all connected flows

elements.name: Or Junction
elements.description: A junction that permits one or more connected flows

relationships.name: Composition
relationships.description: The source consists of the target and the target depends on the source

relationships.name: Assignment
relationships.description: The source allocates responsibility, performance, storage, or execution to the target

relationships.name: Realization
relationships.description: The source plays a critical role in creating, achieving, sustaining, or operating the target

relationships.name: Serving
relationships.description: The source provides its functionality to the target

relationships.name: Access
relationships.description: The source observes or acts upon the target passive structure

relationships.name: Influence
relationships.description: The source affects the implementation or achievement of the target motivation element

relationships.name: Triggering
relationships.description: A temporal or causal relationship between source and target

relationships.name: Flow
relationships.description: Transfer from the source to the target

relationships.name: Specialization
relationships.description: The source is a particular kind of the target

relationships.name: Association
relationships.description: An unspecified relationship not represented by another relationship type
